subject: Post-call qualification + bake-off requests (stack, targets, next steps)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Lila Morgan <lila@cloudnative.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: goals, pain points, and bake-off asks

Hi Lila — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps so we can align before the eval kickoff. Please correct anything I have wrong.

High-level pain points you shared
- End-user latency spikes during peak batch jobs (~p95 > 1.8s) and inconsistent tail latency across regions.
- Cost unpredictability with current self-hosted GPU fleet (vCPU+GPU orchestration overhead).
- Model quality regressions when we parallelize across shards (context fragmentation).

Current stack & constraints
- On-prem Kubernetes (EKS-like) + custom autoscaler; inference currently runs on vLLM builds and a handful of TGI-managed endpoints for DR.
- Data residency requirement: logs + audit traces must remain in their VPC for 30 days.
- Procurement note: PO & SOC2 evidence required before long-running dedicated capacity.

Your success criteria (as we understood)
- Latency: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 600ms for conversational flows at your steady-state traffic.
- Throughput: sustain 120 tokens/sec per node with predictable scaling to 10k concurrent short chats.
- Accuracy/quality: parity or better vs your existing vLLM baseline on the in-house prompt set (we'll use the sample_prompts.csv you shared).
- Cost target: <= 40% of your current cost for equivalent QPS under a production profile.

Bake-off / benchmark asks we proposed
1) Latency curves (p50/p90/p95/p99) across sequence lengths [64, 256, 1024].
2) Tail behavior under simulated region failover (1 node out).
3) Token throughput with batching settings 8/16/32.
4) Quality regressions: accuracy + hallucination rates on your test prompts (we'll run identical prompts against vLLM and TGI cloud).
5) Cost modeling: tokens-per-second cost and effective cost for your target workload (1M token projection).

What we need from you before we start
- Confirm the traffic profile you want us to emulate (steady-state QPS, burst size, session length).
- Approve sharing the sample_prompts.csv and the baseline_metrics_template.xlsx (attached).
- Confirm whether you want the first run in your VPC (preferred) or on our hosted environment (faster to start but requires redaction).

Proposed next steps
- We prepare a test harness and run an initial baseline against vLLM/TGI/cloud on our side (3 business days) unless you prefer private VPC testing.
- Schedule a sandbox bake-off week (we proposed Apr 12-16) — please confirm availability.
- I'll loop Legal for the procurement checklist and SOC2 evidence; Marissa will lead that thread.

If the items above look right, reply with: (A) traffic profile, (B) confirmation of attachment sharing, and (C) preferred environment for the first run (VPC vs hosted).

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182
https://redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: sample_prompts.csv, baseline_metrics_template.xlsx, mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf
From: Lila Morgan <lila@cloudnative.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: goals, pain points, and bake-off asks

Thanks Connor — that summary is very close. Couple clarifications and one ask from my side.

Clarifications
- Steady-state: 450 concurrent short sessions (avg 18 tokens/turn, 3 turns/session) — bursting to ~1,600 sessions during business-hour peaks.
- Our p95 target is aggressive for the whole flow (client-side + server); for bake-off, please measure server-side processing only.

Priority metrics (in order)
1) p95 server-side latency across sequence lengths (we'll prioritize 64 and 256).
2) Worst-case tail when a mid-zone is lost (regional failover).
3) Cost per 1M tokens delivered under our steady-state profile.
4) Quality parity on our prompt set (we'll share 200 eval prompts).

Procurement constraint
- We need a short technical statement listing required SOC2 artifacts and a contact at Legal/Compliance.

Benchmark environment
- We prefer the first full run inside our VPC (private access to sample data). Can you confirm Redwood has a private deployment package for short-term evaluation? If not, we'll accept a hosted run for the initial latency/throughput pass.

Attached I included a condensed test matrix (sample_prompts.csv) — use that for the initial quality pass. I also attached a quick doc outlining the procurement path.

Confirming availability: Apr 12-16 looks good; we can dedicate two engineers (SRE + ML infra) on the 13th and 14th for the live runs.

Thanks — Lila
Lila Morgan
Head of Platform Reliability | CloudNative AI
lila@cloudnative.ai | +1 650-555-0199
